title: fix: activitypub s2s requests fail with 'can only call allowed HTTP servers'
body:
This (untested!) patch hopefully fixes federation issues I encountered with the current v16 release. Other ActivityPub (Mastodon) servers were unable to find profiles on my Forgejo instance because the request to `/api/v1/activitypub/user-id/1` failed with a 400 "request signature verification failed" error. Tracelogs showed that the answer is a lie, Forgejo did in fact successfully verified the HTTP header signature of the request, but then triggered an unrelated error while trying to fetch `.well-known/nodeinfo` from the remote server. The logged error message was "activitypub can only call allowed HTTP servers (check your  setting)", but the allowed hosts are not actually configured in settings, they are set by the `APClientFactory` subclass of `ClientFactory` by extracting the `URL.Host` from the target URL.

This is the actual bug. `URL.Host` may contain a port suffix, but `HostMatchList` checks patterns against target hostnames without a port. A request to `https://mastodon.social:443/.well-known/nodeinfo` fails because `"mastodon.social:443" != "mastodon.social"`.

I am not a go developer and I do not have a test environment in place, so this is completely untested. I ran `make pr-go` though and it didn't complain.
